chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Reaction to Afro-Cuban jazz and the Carnegie Hall date
summary: Audiences raved about the polyrhythm of conga, bongo and timbales, then Carnegie Hall followed with Sonny Stitt replacing Charlie Parker.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah, right. It was the first concert of its type; but did a lot of people or did you get any
feedback, that they realized what was going on? That that was the first time Afro-Cuban jazz was formally introduced to the public? Was there anything written about that, was there any feedback?

Well, the peole start to rave about the commotion of our rhythm section create because they knew about jazz, but they never had that in a battle. The jazz was played by a bass and a drummer and the usual jazz; but, and then when you put a conga and bongo and timbales and maracas and senserro or cow bells, you know, there are so many syn-copation involved that the people they just went crazy.
From there we went to the Carnegie Hall where we were supposed to play for Charlie Parker, but Charlie Parker got sick and was replaced by Sonny Stitt.
